intro: Probability is a fraction: **the ways you want, out of all the ways**. Everything after that is counting, which Permutations & Combinations has already taught.
There are eight short lessons. Go in order the first time.

**What the papers ask.** Two IBPS Clerk papers in the sample had one question each: 2018 (two balls from a bag, after finding a count) and Dec 2021 (two balls of one colour). None of the 2022 to 2025 Clerk papers checked, and none of the 12 sister papers (2025-26), had one. Light insurance for Clerk Prelims.
Practice questions are from the Guidely bank; every answer used was re-computed with exact fractions.
after: That is the whole topic. The **Quick revision** tab has the rules on one page.

lessons.title: Favourable out of all
lessons.plain: The starting point: probability is a fraction. Count what you want, count everything, divide.
teach: **Probability = favourable outcomes / all outcomes**, when every outcome is equally likely. It is always between 0 and 1.
A die has 6 faces; the primes are 2, 3, 5: probability 3/6 = 1/2.
A pack has 52 cards: 4 suits (hearts and diamonds red, clubs and spades black) of 13 cards each; 4 kings, 4 queens, 4 jacks, 4 aces.
**Not** is 1 minus: neither a king nor a queen is 1 - 8/52 = 11/13.
Numbers from 1 to n divisible by d: count them as the whole part of n / d.

example.q: A ball is drawn from balls numbered 1 to 40. What is the probability that its number divides by 6?

check.q: A card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a red king?
check.why: Two red kings out of 52: 2/52 = 1/26. (1/13 counts all four kings.)

lessons.title: Coins and dice: list the outcomes
lessons.plain: New: several coins or dice at once. Count all outcomes by multiplying, then the ones you want.
teach: n coins give 2 x 2 x ... = 2ⁿ outcomes; two dice give 6 x 6 = 36.
**Exactly r heads in n tosses:** nCr of the 2ⁿ outcomes. 3 coins, exactly 2 heads: 3C2 = 3 of 8.
**At least one head:** 1 - (all tails) = 1 - 1/2ⁿ.
Two dice: list the sums. Sum 7 comes 6 ways; 6 and 8 come 5 ways each; 2 and 12 one way each.

example.q: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 9 or more?

check.q: Four coins are tossed. What is the probability of exactly 2 heads?
check.why: 4C2 = 6 of 16 outcomes: 6/16 = 3/8. (1/2 assumes heads and tails just split evenly.)

lessons.title: Drawing two or three from a bag
lessons.plain: New: several items are drawn at once. Count with selections.
teach: Drawing 2 balls at once: all outcomes = nC2 for n balls. Favourable = selections of the kind wanted.
2 green from 3 red and 4 green: 4C2 / 7C2 = 6/21 = 2/7.
**Different colours** (one of each): multiply the counts: 5 red x 6 blue = 30 of 11C2 = 55.
Cards the same way: 2 red cards: 26C2 / 52C2 = 325 / 1,326 = 25/102.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2018 and Dec 2021 each set one bag question.

example.q: A bag has 12 blue balls and 8 others that are yellow or pink. The probability of drawing a yellow ball is 1/4. Two balls are drawn. What is the probability both are pink?

check.q: A bag has 5 red and 5 green balls. Two are drawn. What is the probability both are red?
check.why: 5C2 / 10C2 = 10/45 = 2/9. (1/4 is (1/2) x (1/2), which forgets the first ball is not put back.) IBPS Clerk Dec 2021 asked this form.

tags: Exactly two of one kind in three.

lessons.title: Same colour, or this or that: add the cases
lessons.plain: New: more than one kind of outcome is wanted. Count each kind and add.
teach: "Both the same colour" = both red + both blue + ... Each is a separate count; add them before dividing.
"Either both red or both blue" works the same way.
Three of the same colour from 4 pink, 6 grey and 4 brown: 4C3 + 6C3 + 4C3 = 4 + 20 + 4 = 28 of 14C3 = 364.

example.q: A bag has 3 red, 4 green and 5 blue balls. Two are drawn. What is the probability they are the same colour?
steps: Both red 3, both green 6, both blue 10: 19.

check.q: A box has 4 red and 3 green balls. Two are drawn. What is the probability they are the same colour?

tags: Either both red or both blue.

lessons.title: At least and at most
lessons.plain: New: the quickest route is often the opposite event.
teach: **At least one** = 1 - (none). At least one red in 3 from 5 red and 10 others: 1 - 10C3 / 15C3.
**At most two** of 3 = 1 - (all three).
When the opposite is no shorter, add the cases directly, as in P&C.

example.q: Two balls are drawn from 4 red and 6 white. What is the probability of at least one red?

check.q: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of at most two heads?
check.why: All three heads is 1/8, so at most two is 7/8. (3/8 is exactly two.)

tags: At most two women: add the cases.

lessons.title: A count is missing
lessons.plain: New: the probability is given and a number of balls is asked.
teach: Write the probability with the unknown and match it: green 5 of a total T is 1/3, so T = 15.
With two drawn, the match is with selections: two blue = 4C2 / nC2 = 2/7 gives nC2 = 21, so n = 7.
Try the options when the equation looks awkward: they are small whole numbers.

example.q: A bag has x red and 6 blue balls. The probability of drawing a red ball is 1/4. Find x.

check.q: A bag has 9 balls; 3 are red. One more red ball is added. What is the probability of drawing red now?
check.why: 4 red of 10: 2/5. (1/3 is before the ball was added.)

lessons.title: One after another: with or without putting back
lessons.plain: New: draws happen in turn. Multiply the probabilities of each step.
teach: **With replacement:** each draw has the same chances. First prime (10 of 30) and then a square (5 of 30): 1/3 x 1/6 = 1/18.
**Without replacement:** the second draw has one fewer item. First white (12 of 28), then black (16 of 27): 12/28 x 16/27.
"Both the same" with replacement: add the squares of each kind's chance.
At least two of three draws with replacement: (exactly two) + (all three), using 3C2 for which draws.

example.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two are drawn one by one without replacement. What is the probability both are red?

check.q: A die is rolled twice. What is the probability of a 6 both times?
check.why: 1/6 x 1/6 = 1/36. (1/12 adds the chances instead of multiplying.)

lessons.title: Either, neither, and overlaps
lessons.plain: New: two events that can share outcomes.
teach: **Either A or B** = A + B - (both), so a shared outcome is not counted twice. A club or a jack: 13 + 4 - 1 = 16 of 52.
**Neither A nor B** = 1 - (either).
If A and B cannot happen together (a queen of clubs or a king of hearts), just add.

example.q: A card is drawn. What is the probability it is a heart or a king?
steps: Hearts 13, kings 4, the king of hearts counted twice: 13 + 4 - 1 = 16.

check.q: A number is chosen from 1 to 20. What is the probability it is even or a multiple of 5?
check.why: Even 10, multiples of 5 are 4, both (10, 20) 2: 12/20 = 3/5. (7/10 forgets to remove the overlap.)

probability-based-on-either-or-neither-s: Neither red nor blue means black: 8 of 32.
probability-based-on-balls-set-1-prelims: 7/15 is not among the options, so the answer is None of these.
11/45 is not among the options, so the answer is None of these.
probability-based-on-dice-set-1-prelims-: Equal pairs: 6 of 36. The other 30 split evenly: 15 with the second higher.
probability-based-on-same-or-different-c: Both red 6, both green 15, both blue 1: 22.
probability-based-on-atleast-or-atmost-s: No apple means both oranges: 1 of 10.
probability-based-on-variables-set-1-pre: Green 4 is 2/5 of the total, so the total is 10.
probability-based-on-with-replacement-se: Red chance 10/35 = 2/7. Exactly two: 3 x (2/7)² x 5/7 = 60/343. All three: 8/343.
probability-based-on-cards-set-1-prelims: Queen of clubs or king of hearts: 2 cards.
probability-based-on-dice-set-1-prelims-: Sum 5: 4 ways; 10: 3 ways; 7: 6 ways. No sum is both.
